Blended generalized Pareto distribution functions

bgpd.Rd

Distribution utilities for the blended generalized Pareto construction of Majumder and Richards (2026). A finite-support bulk model on \([0,1]\) is blended with a GP tail using the paper's multiplicative CDF blend and Beta-CDF weighting function.

Usage

pbgpd(
  q,
  xi,
  pbulk = pbeta,
  dbulk = dbeta,
  qbulk = qbeta,
  bulk.args = list(shape1 = 2, shape2 = 5),
  pa = 0.8,
  pb = 0.99,
  c1 = 5,
  c2 = 5
)

dbgpd(
  x,
  xi,
  pbulk = pbeta,
  dbulk = dbeta,
  qbulk = qbeta,
  bulk.args = list(shape1 = 2, shape2 = 5),
  pa = 0.8,
  pb = 0.99,
  c1 = 5,
  c2 = 5,
  log = FALSE
)

qbgpd(
  p,
  xi,
  pbulk = pbeta,
  dbulk = dbeta,
  qbulk = qbeta,
  bulk.args = list(shape1 = 2, shape2 = 5),
  pa = 0.8,
  pb = 0.99,
  c1 = 5,
  c2 = 5
)

rbgpd(
  n,
  xi,
  pbulk = pbeta,
  dbulk = dbeta,
  qbulk = qbeta,
  bulk.args = list(shape1 = 2, shape2 = 5),
  pa = 0.8,
  pb = 0.99,
  c1 = 5,
  c2 = 5,
  unifsamp = NULL
)

Arguments

q

quantiles.

xi

GP tail shape parameter.

pbulk

bulk CDF supported on \([0,1]\).

dbulk

bulk density supported on \([0,1]\). It is also used to numerically validate the blended construction.

qbulk

bulk quantile function supported on \([0,1]\).

bulk.args

named list of arguments passed to pbulk, dbulk, and qbulk. The default corresponds to a Beta bulk.

pa

lower bulk quantile where blending starts.

pb

upper bulk quantile where blending ends and the exact GP tail begins.

c1, c2

shape parameters of the Beta weighting function used for blending.

x

values.

log

logical; should log-densities be returned?

p

probabilities.

n

number of samples.

unifsamp

optional uniforms to transform instead of drawing new ones.

Value

pbgpd() returns CDF values.

dbgpd() returns density values.

qbgpd() returns quantiles.

rbgpd() returns random draws.

Details

The GP threshold and scale are derived from pa and pb so that the blended CDF matches the bulk CDF at the start and end of the blending interval. For \(y \le a\), the distribution equals the bulk model; for \(y \ge b\), it equals the exact GP model.

Because the paper notes that some bulk/weight combinations can produce a negative density in the blending interval, these helpers numerically screen the blended density over that interval and stop if the supplied specification appears invalid.

Examples

## Default Beta-bulk blended GP
pbgpd(c(0.2, 0.8, 1.5), xi = 0.2)
#> [1] 0.3446400 0.9950300 0.9998319
dbgpd(c(0.2, 0.8, 1.5), xi = 0.2)
#> [1] 2.4576000000 0.0343835799 0.0005908393
qbgpd(c(0.5, 0.9, 0.99), xi = 0.2)
#> [1] 0.2644500 0.5065306 0.7056863

## Custom bulk distribution on [0, 1]
qbgpd(
  c(0.5, 0.9, 0.99),
  xi = -0.15,
  pbulk = pbeta,
  dbulk = dbeta,
  qbulk = qbeta,
  bulk.args = list(shape1 = 3, shape2 = 7),
  pa = 0.7,
  pb = 0.95
)
#> [1] 0.2862367 0.4855701 0.6770339
